html:
On 17 April 1961 about 1,400 Cuban exiles, trained and armed by the CIA, landed at the Bay of Pigs on Cuba's south coast to overthrow Fidel Castro. They were defeated within three days.

President John F. Kennedy had approved a plan drawn up under Eisenhower, but refused to send US air cover. The expected rising inside Cuba never came, and most invaders were captured and later ransomed for food and medicine.

The defeat was a triumph for Castro, who declared the revolution socialist on the eve of the landing. It drew Cuba closer to the Soviet Union and helped lead to the Cuban Missile Crisis the next year, a defining moment of the Cold War.
